questions.subject: evs

learning_outcomes.text_as_printed: Define and explain what elements, compounds, and mixtures are.
Classify matter into elements, compounds, and mixtures based on their characteristics.
Understand that elements are made up of atoms having the same properties and cannot be chemically broken down further.
Identify examples of natural and artificial elements.
Explain that compounds are formed when two or more elements chemically combine in a fixed ratio to form a substance with new properties.
Write and interpret molecular formulas that represent the number and type of atoms in a compound (e.g., H₂O for water).
Recognize that the properties of a compound are different from the properties of the elements that form it.
Describe that mixtures consist of two or more substances (elements or compounds) physically mixed without chemical change.
Understand that in mixtures, the individual substances retain their original properties and can be separated by simple physical methods.
Differentiate between compounds and mixtures by comparing their formation, properties, and methods of separation.
Give everyday examples of elements, compounds, and mixtures.
Recognize that elements, compounds, and mixtures can exist in solid, liquid, or gaseous states.
Appreciate the importance of chemical combinations in forming compounds useful in daily life (e.g., salt formed from poisonous sodium and chlorine).
Develop observational and classification skills by examining different substances around them.

Recognize that the properties of a compound are different from the properties of the elements that form it.
Describe that mixtures consist of two or more substances (elements or compounds) physically mixed without chemical change.
Understand that in mixtures, the individual substances retain their original properties and can be separated by simple physical methods.
Differentiate between compounds and mixtures by comparing their formation, properties, and methods of separation.
Give everyday examples of elements, compounds, and mixtures.
Recognize that elements, compounds, and mixtures can exist in solid, liquid, or gaseous states.
Appreciate the importance of chemical combinations in forming compounds useful in daily life (e.g., salt formed from poisonous sodium and chlorine).
Develop observational and classification skills by examining different substances around them.
